items.title: Periodic fluid Fourier Sobolev spaces
items.statement:
**Choice context.** The finite coefficient arrays and weighted coefficient completion below are defined without Countable Choice. In this coefficient-only reading, a finite real trigonometric polynomial is specified by a finite coefficient array $(a_k)$, extended by zero and satisfying $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$, and $\widehat q(k):=a_k$ denotes its specified coefficient coordinate. For the normalized Haar-measure conventions, integral Fourier coefficients and $L^2$ realization below, additionally assume Countable Choice, as in the declared measure and Fourier suppliers. In that analytic context the coefficient coordinates agree with the integral coefficients.

Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $N\ge1$ be integers. Let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ carry the probability measure obtained by pushing normalized Haar measure on $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$ forward under $y\mapsto x=2\pi y$; in coordinates this is $(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For any componentwise integrable real $q:Q_d\to\mathbb R^N$, considered up to equality almost everywhere, and $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, define its componentwise Fourier coefficient by $\widehat q(k)=\int_{Q_d}q(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$; this integral is finite because $|e^{ik\cdot x}|=1$ and $q\in L^1$. A finite real trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum $q(x)=\sum_{k\in F}a_ke^{ik\cdot x}$, where $F\subset\mathbb Z^d$ is finite and the coefficients, extended by zero outside $F$, satisfy $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$. Such polynomials are integrable and satisfy $\widehat q(-k)=\overline{\widehat q(k)}$. Put $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$. For any $s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(Q_d;\mathbb R^N)$ as the completion of finite real trigonometric polynomials in the norm $\|q\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2s}|\widehat q(k)|^2$. Identify this completion with the weighted coefficient space subject to conjugate symmetry, using finite symmetric cutoffs, and write $\widehat q(k)$ for its coefficient coordinate. Under Countable Choice, if $s\ge0$, each element has a unique $L^2$ representative, and its coefficient coordinate agrees with the normalized integral formula; for $s<0$ no $L^2$ representative is asserted.

items.title: Projected no-slip Stokes Hilbert space
items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $R>0$, and let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be a nonempty bounded open set. Define $W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ componentwise: $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_d)$ belongs to it exactly when each $v_i$ belongs to the scalar $W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ defined in the earlier integer-order Sobolev-space definition. Its weak derivatives are $\partial_jv_i$, its gradient is the matrix $
abla v=(\partial_jv_i)_{i,j=1}^d$, and its norm is
$$\|v\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)}^2=\sum_{i=1}^d\left(\|v_i\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=1}^d\|\partial_jv_i\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2ight)=\int_\Omega\left(|v|^2+|
abla v|_F^2ight)\,dx,$$
where $v\cdot w=\sum_i v_iw_i$, $|v|^2=\sum_i|v_i|^2$, $A:B=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$, and $|A|_F^2=\sum_{i,j}|A_{ij}|^2$. Define $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as the closure of the $d$-tuples of compactly supported smooth real functions in this norm. Define $\operatorname{div}v=0$ distributionally to mean $\int_\Omega v\cdot
abla\phi=0$ for every $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and set $V=\{v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d):\operatorname{div}v=0\}$. Equip $V$ with the inherited $H^1$ inner product $\int_\Omega(v\cdot w+
abla v:
abla w)$. The phrase no-slip here means membership in this closure; no trace characterization on arbitrary $\Omega$ is part of the definition.

items.title: Rectangular continuous divergence inverse on mean-zero tests
items.statement: Let $d\ge1$ and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(a_i,b_i)$ be a nonempty finite open rectangle. Write $D(\Omega)=C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and $D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in D(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$. For every compact $K\subset\Omega$ there is a compact $K'\subset\Omega$ such that a linear map $R:D_0(\Omega)\to D(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ sends tests supported in $K$ to fields supported in $K'$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}(Rh)=h$, and is continuous on each fixed-support test space for the seminorms $\sup|\partial^\alpha h|$.

items.title: Periodic Fourier embeddings and products
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and use $H^\sigma(Q_d)$ with the normalized measure and weights in the Definition. For every integer $j\ge0$ and $\sigma>j+d/2$, each scalar $q\in H^\sigma(Q_d)$ has a $C^j$ representative and $\|q\|_{C^j}\le C_{d,\sigma,j}\|q\|_{H^\sigma}$. For every $\sigma>d/2$, pointwise multiplication extends uniquely from trigonometric polynomials to a continuous bilinear map $H^\sigma\times H^\sigma\to H^\sigma$ satisfying $\|fg\|_{H^\sigma}\le C_{d,\sigma}\|f\|_{H^\sigma}\|g\|_{H^\sigma}$. The assertions extend componentwise to finite-dimensional vector and tensor fields.

items.title: Periodic Leray and pressure maps
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and fix $d\in\{1,2,3\}$. For a vector Fourier coefficient $a(k)\in\mathbb C^d$, define $(Pa)(k)=P_ka(k)$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, where $P_0=I$ and $P_k=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2$ for $k
e0$. For a tensor field $F=(F_{ij})_{i,j=1}^d$ with coefficients in any $H^s(Q_d)$, define the scalar pressure map $Q$ by $\widehat{QF}(0)=0$ and $\widehat{QF}(k)=-\sum_{i,j=1}^d k_i k_j|k|^{-2}\widehat F_{ij}(k)$ for $k
e0$. For $q\in H^s(Q_d)$, define $\partial_jq\in H^{s-1}(Q_d)$ coefficientwise by $\widehat{\partial_jq}(k)=ik_j\widehat q(k)$; for vector fields set $\widehat{
abla q}(k)=ik\widehat q(k)$, and for tensor fields set $\widehat{\operatorname{div}F}_i(k)=i\sum_jk_j\widehat F_{ij}(k)$. These derivative maps are bounded from $H^s$ to $H^{s-1}$. The multipliers $P$ and $Q$ are real-preserving and bounded on every $H^s$, $s\in\mathbb R$; $P$ is an orthogonal projection and commutes with these derivatives. For every $F$ and every $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, their exact identity is the coefficientwise equality
$$\widehat{
abla QF}(k)=-(I-P_k)\widehat{\operatorname{div}F}(k).$$
In particular, both sides have zero coefficient at $k=0$.

items.title: Tame transport commutator
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $m\ge s\ge4$ be integers, let $f,g\in C^\infty(Q_d;\mathbb R)$, and define $\Lambda^m$ by $\widehat{\Lambda^m q}(k)=w_k^m\widehat q(k)$. For each coordinate $j$,
$$\|[\Lambda^m,f]\partial_jg\|_{L^2}\le C_{d,m,s}\bigl(\|f\|_{H^m}\|g\|_{H^s}+\|f\|_{H^s}\|g\|_{H^m}\bigr),$$
where $[\Lambda^m,f]h=\Lambda^m(fh)-f\Lambda^mh$.

items.title: Pressure recovery for periodic incompressible Sobolev velocity
items.statement:
Let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ have normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in\mathbb N_0^d$, write $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$ and $\partial^\alpha=\partial_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots\partial_d^{\alpha_d}$. Give $C^\infty(Q_d;\mathbb R)$ the Fr'echet topology generated by $p_m(\phi)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\|\partial^\alpha\phi\|_\infty$, for $m\in\mathbb N_0$, where the derivatives are those of the smooth periodic lift to $\mathbb R^d$. A periodic distribution is a continuous real-linear functional on this test space, extended complex-linearly to complex-valued tests. For such a distribution $S$, define $\widehat S(k)=\langle S,e^{-ik\cdot x}angle$ for $e_k(x)=e^{ik\cdot x}$ and define its mean to be $\widehat S(0)=\langle S,1angle$. For an integrable function $g$, the pairing is $\langle g,\phiangle=\int_{Q_d}g\phi\,d\mu$. Define distributional derivatives by $\langle\partial_jS,\phiangle=-\langle S,\partial_j\phiangle$. For a smooth scalar test, $
abla\phi=(\partial_1\phi,\ldots,\partial_d\phi)$ and $\Delta\phi=\sum_j\partial_j^2\phi$; for a smooth vector field $v$, $\operatorname{div}v=\sum_j\partial_jv_j$, $(v\otimes v)_{ij}=v_iv_j$, and $(v\cdot
abla)v_i=\sum_jv_j\partial_jv_i$. In particular, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ distributionally means $-\int_{Q_d}u\cdot
abla\phi\,d\mu=0$ for every real test function $\phi$. Equality of periodic distributions means equality on every such test function. Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $s>d/2+1$, and let $u\in H^s(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfy $\operatorname{div}u=0$ in this sense. Then $u\otimes u\in H^s$, the mean-zero scalar $\pi=Q(u\otimes u)$ belongs to $H^s$, and in $H^{s-1}$,
$$P(u\cdot
abla u)=u\cdot
abla u+
abla\pi.$$
Among mean-zero periodic distributions $\widetilde\pi$ for which this identity holds as an equality of periodic distributions, this pressure is unique. The formula is a torus pressure recovery result and asserts no wall pressure regularity.

items.title: Directional Poincaré bound for zero trace
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, $R>0$, and let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be bounded and open. For every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$,
$$\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le2R\|\partial_1v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le2R\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
Here $H_0^1$ is the closure of compactly supported smooth fields in the Sobolev norm.

items.title: Projected stationary weak Stokes solvability
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, let $R>0$, let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be nonempty bounded open, let $\mu>0$, and let $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$. There is a unique $u\in V$ such that
$$\mu\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v=\int_\Omega f\cdot v\qquad(v\in V),$$
where $V$ is the distributionally divergence-free subspace of $H_0^1$ defined above. It satisfies $\|
abla u\|_2\le2R\|f\|_2/\mu$. This is a projected variational velocity result; it asserts no pressure, $L^2$ pressure regularity, or classical boundary regularity.

items.title: Difference energy for given smooth incompressible and symmetric solutions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $T>0$, and $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For $z:Q_d\to\mathbb R^M$, use componentwise Fourier coefficients $\widehat z(k)=\int_{Q_d}z(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, weights $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$, and the weighted coefficient completion norm $\|z\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2s}|\widehat z(k)|^2$; the normalized Fourier isometry gives $\|z\|_2^2=\sum_k|\widehat z(k)|^2$, where $\|z\|_2=(\int_{Q_d}|z|^2\,d\mu)^{1/2}$ and the pointwise component norm is Euclidean. In particular, $H^0=L^2$. For a map $z:[0,T]\times Q_d\to\mathbb R^M$, smooth on the closed cylinder means that for every $m\in\mathbb N_0$ and spatial multi-index $\alpha$, $\partial_t^m\partial_x^\alpha z$ exists on $(0,T)\times Q_d$ and extends continuously to $[0,T]\times Q_d$; spatial derivatives are those of its periodic lift. For a spatial vector field define $\operatorname{div}z=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jz_j$ and $\Delta z=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j^2z$. Write $\nabla z$ for the spatial Jacobian and $\|\nabla z(t)\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in Q_d}|\nabla z(t,x)|_F$, where $|\cdot|_F$ is the Euclidean Frobenius matrix norm. Let $P$ be the coefficientwise vector multiplier with $P_0=I$ and $P_k=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2$ for $k\ne0$. The equations below hold pointwise on $(0,T)\times Q_d$ and at the time endpoints by continuous extension.

(i) If $\nu\ge0$ and $u,v\in C^\infty([0,T]\times Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfy, for each $z\in\{u,v\}$,
$$z_t+P((z\cdot\nabla)z)=\nu\Delta z,\qquad \operatorname{div}z=0,$$
then for every $t\in[0,T]$, with $w=u-v$,
$$\|w(t)\|_2^2\le\|w(0)\|_2^2\exp\!\left(2\int_0^t\|\nabla v(\tau)\|_\infty\,d\tau\right).$$

(ii) Let $N\ge1$ and, for $1\le j\le d$, let $A_j:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ be a fixed real-linear map whose image consists of symmetric matrices. If $q,r\in C^\infty([0,T]\times Q_d;\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy, for each $z\in\{q,r\}$,
$$z_t+\sum_{j=1}^dA_j(z)\partial_jz=0,$$
then for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|q(t)-r(t)\|_2^2\le\|q(0)-r(0)\|_2^2\exp\!\left(C_{d,N,A}\int_0^t(\|\nabla q(\tau)\|_\infty+\|\nabla r(\tau)\|_\infty)\,d\tau\right),$$
where $C_{d,N,A}$ depends only on $d,N$ and the operator norms of the finitely many maps $A_j$. For either pair $(z_1,z_2)=(u,v)$ or $(q,r)$, put $w=z_1-z_2$. Let $\Gamma\ge0$ be any uniform rate for which the corresponding squared $L^2$ estimate above gives $\|w(t)\|_2^2\le\|w(0)\|_2^2e^{\Gamma t}$. If $s\ge1$ and $\max_{t\in[0,T]}\max(\|z_1(t)\|_{H^s},\|z_2(t)\|_{H^s})\le M$ for some $M\ge0$, define
$$B_s(M)=\begin{cases}1,&s=1,\\(2M)^{(s-1)/s},&s>1.\end{cases}$$
Then for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|w(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le B_s(M)\|w(0)\|_2^{1/s}e^{\Gamma t/(2s)}.$$
These are conditional estimates for already given smooth maps on the stated cylinder and assert no existence theorem. All quantities are mathematical and no physical units are assigned to $\nu$.

items.title: Rectangular no-slip Stokes velocity and distribution pressure
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, $R>0$, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(a_i,b_i)\subset(-R,R)^d$ be a nonempty finite open rectangle. For $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in\mathbb N_0^d$, write $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$ and $\partial^\alpha=\partial_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots\partial_d^{\alpha_d}$. For each compact $K\subset\Omega$, let $\mathcal D_K(\Omega)=\{\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):\operatorname{supp}\phi\subseteq K\}$ with seminorms $p_{K,m}(\phi)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in K}|\partial^\alpha\phi(x)|$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$. Give $\mathcal D(\Omega)=C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)= igcup_{K	ext{ compact},\ K\subset\Omega}\mathcal D_K(\Omega)$ the locally convex inductive-limit topology of these fixed-support test spaces. Give vector test fields the componentwise topology. A scalar or vector distribution is a continuous real-linear functional on the corresponding test space; write its bilinear real pairing as $\langle T,\phiangle$ or $\langle T,\psiangle$. For scalar distributions define $\langle\partial_jT,\phiangle=-\langle T,\partial_j\phiangle$. For a smooth vector field $\psi=(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_d)$, set $\operatorname{div}\psi=\sum_j\partial_j\psi_j$ and $\langle
abla p,\psiangle=-\langle p,\operatorname{div}\psiangle$. An $L^2$ vector field $f$ acts by $\langle f,\psiangle=\int_\Omega f\cdot\psi\,dx$, and for $u\in H_0^1$ define $\langle\Delta u,\psiangle=-\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla\psi\,dx$. Here, for $m=1$ or $m=d$, $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$ is the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$ in $\|v\|_{H^1}=(\int_\Omega(|v|^2+|
abla v|^2)\,dx)^{1/2}$, where $(
abla v)_{ij}=\partial_jv_i$ and $A:B=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$; $H^{-1}(\Omega)=(H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R))'$ is the continuous real dual of the scalar space with dual norm $\|p\|_{H^{-1}}=\sup_{\|\phi\|_{H^1}\le1}|\langle p,\phiangle|$. A constant distribution $c$ acts by $\langle c,\phiangle=c\int_\Omega\phi\,dx$; $\mathbb R\subset H^{-1}$ denotes this subspace, and $H^{-1}/\mathbb R$ has quotient norm $\|[p]\|=\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\|p-c\|_{H^{-1}}$. Thus $D'(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ denotes the continuous real dual of the vector test space, and the equation below is an equality on every vector test field. Define $V=\{v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d):\int_\Omega v\cdot
abla\phi\,dx=0	ext{ for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)\}$, with the inherited $H^1$ norm.

Let $\mu>0$ and $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$. There is a unique $u\in V$ such that
$$\mu\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v\,dx=\int_\Omega f\cdot v\,dx\qquad(v\in V),$$
and $\|
abla u\|_2\le2R\|f\|_2/\mu$. There is a distribution $p\in H^{-1}(\Omega)$ such that $-\mu\Delta u+
abla p=f$ in $D'(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$; it is unique modulo constant distributions. With the quotient norm on $H^{-1}/\mathbb R$ and the product of the inherited $H^1$ norm on $V$ with that quotient norm, the map $f\mapsto(u,[p])$ into $V	imes(H^{-1}/\mathbb R)$ is bounded and linear. The pressure is not asserted to lie in $L^2$ or to be smooth at rectangle corners.

items.title: Shear mode has zero periodic pressure
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $A\in\mathbb R$, and $u(x)=A\sin(x_2)e_1$ on $Q_d$, where $e_1$ is the first coordinate vector. Then $u$ is smooth and divergence-free, $u\cdot\nabla u=0$, and its unique mean-zero pressure recovered by $Q(u\otimes u)$ is $\pi=0$. This is a verification of the pressure recovery map; it is not asserted to solve an unforced viscous Navier–Stokes equation.

items.title: Full wall Stokes pressure requires a divergence inverse
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, $R>0$, and let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be a nonempty bounded open set. For each $\mu>0$ and $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, the projected stationary Stokes theorem gives a unique $u$ in the distributionally divergence-free subspace $V$ of the closure-based $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ space, satisfying
$$\mu\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v\,dx=\int_\Omega f\cdot v\,dx\qquad(v\in V),$$
with $\|
abla u\|_2\le2R\|f\|_2/\mu$; this conclusion contains no pressure. If $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(a_i,b_i)\subset(-R,R)^d$ is a nonempty finite open rectangle, the separate rectangular theorem additionally gives $p\in H^{-1}(\Omega)$ such that $-\mu\Delta u+
abla p=f$ as vector distributions, with $p$ unique modulo constant distributions. The rectangular result does not assert an $L^2$ pressure estimate or smoothness at rectangle corners. Neither theorem claims pressure recovery for arbitrary bounded open sets; such a claim needs a domain-appropriate divergence right inverse or inf-sup argument.
